Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. 

The Asset Movements Operations team at Robinhood is dedicated to offering fast, safe, and secure execution of customer requests such as wires, checks, and internal account transfers. As a critical pillar of Robinhood's brokerage business model, our team focuses on risk management and operational accuracy to support the firm's growth. We collaborate with Customer Experience, Clearing, Fraud, and Financial Crimes teams to troubleshoot complex issues and ensure seamless processing. Our culture thrives on teamwork, continuous improvement, and a shared dedication to protecting our customers' assets. Together, we are building the future of retail brokerage operations!

As an Asset Movements Operations Specialist, you will play a central role in executing daily financial transactions with precision and resolving customer requests. In this position, you will be accountable for high-priority wire, check, and journal processing while identifying operational inefficiencies. You will collaborate with project and operations teams to launch and scale Robinhood's electronic financial products. Your analytical skills will be key in mitigating money movement risks and safeguarding customer and firm assets. This is an exciting opportunity to help build our brokerage infrastructure and grow your career with us!

This role is based in our Denver, CO or Westlake, TX office , with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week (Wednesday, Thursday and Friday). 

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. 

What you’ll do

  • Process high-priority transactions, including wires, checks, journals, and bank-linking, ensuring accuracy and timely completion.
  • Evaluate and manage money movement risks from both a customer and firm perspective to mitigate financial losses.
  • Collaborate with project and operations teams to test, launch, and scale retail brokerage products and operational systems.
  • Develop and document operational processes and procedures to improve efficiency and maintain compliance standards.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert in asset movements, collaborating with Customer Experience, Clearing, Fraud, and Financial Crimes teams to resolve complex customer issues.

What you bring

  • A Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, business, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience), along with 4+ years of experience in brokerage operations or financial services.
  • Active FINRA Series 7 license; an active FINRA Series 24 license is preferred.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a demonstrated ability to identify process inefficiencies, propose concrete solutions, and manage operational risk.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to explain complex operational and compliance concepts clearly.
  • Exceptional attention to detail, deep knowledge of banking operation standards, and advanced familiarity with securities industry compliance policies.

What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career
  • Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching
  • Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents
  • Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not
  • Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more
  • Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits
  • Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more!
  • Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces.

In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits.

descriptions.job-14s1xf3:
About Dakota

Dakota is a stablecoin infrastructure platform powering modern financial products through regulated money movement, stablecoin orchestration, and cross-border settlement. We serve institutional clients — fintechs, payment service providers, marketplaces, and enterprises — through an API-first platform that abstracts the complexity of custody, compliance, settlement, and banking partnerships.

We are a remote first team across North America and Europe. We value high quality work, clear thinking and ownership.

Key responsibilities

Financial risk and advisory

  • Serve as senior FCC point of contact and SME on fiat and digital assets; contribute to the FCC framework.

  • Identify and assess money laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions, fraud and other illicit finance risks across digital asset products, clients, counterparties and transaction flows, including blockchain, wallets, custody models, and stablecoins.

  • Provide risk-based advice and effective challenge across the product and client lifecycle: new initiatives, product approvals, onboarding and material changes.

  • Assess cross-business and cross-regional impacts, promoting consistent minimum standards and documented treatment of regional variances.

Controls and program oversight

  • Partner with first-line and other teams to design, enhance and oversee controls for CDD/EDD and KYC, sanctions screening, blockchain analytics, transaction monitoring, case management, investigations, suspicious activity escalation and recordkeeping.

  • Review AML programs and internal control structures, including automated solutions, through policy and procedure reviews, gap analyses, risk assessments and regulatory compliance assessments.

  • Identify and escalate material risks and control weaknesses, and oversee agreed remediation.

FCC technology, models and data

  • Lead implementation of FCC technology solutions, including onboarding blockchain analytics and digital asset intelligence vendors and managing vendor relationships.

  • Develop transaction monitoring scenarios aligned to products, services and risk appetite.

  • Lead testing, tuning and optimization of transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, customer risk rating and detection, before production and on an ongoing basis.

  • Validate AML models across those same areas.

  • Perform and oversee data reconciliation, lineage and quality testing; interpret complex analyses to identify patterns, risks and conclusions.

  • Improve data quality, system capabilities and automation to strengthen preventive and detective controls.

Regulatory engagement and governance

  • Monitor new laws, regulations, guidance, enforcement actions and industry practice, and translate them into practical requirements and action plans.

  • Support engagement with regulators, auditors and independent reviewers, including exam preparation, information requests and remediation of findings, as necessary.

  • Develop policies, procedures, training, metrics, and governance materials for senior stakeholders and committees.

Leadership and relationships

  • Lead multiple complex FCC initiatives from initiation to completion, on time, within budget and to stakeholder expectations.

  • Manage teams, delegating effectively to managers and mentoring junior and mid-level staff, while still being hands-on.

  • Build strong relationships with executives, business, technology, Risk and Audit partners, and industry forums or trade associations.

  • Lead stakeholder discussions, identify new opportunities to add value, and deliver special projects as assigned.

Qualifications

  • 7+ years in Financial Crime Compliance, Compliance, Legal, Risk, Internal Audit or a related control function, preferably at a financial institution or regulated digital assets business.

  • Practical experience in legal, financial, technical, risk or compliance background is preferred.

  • Deep knowledge of AML, CTF, sanctions and fraud risk frameworks, including CDD, transaction monitoring, investigations, regulatory reporting and common typologies.

  • Working knowledge of blockchain and digital assets, or experience assessing financial crime risk in new products, technologies or payment models.

  • Track record building controls for digital assets risk, including work with blockchain analytics vendors.

  • Experience conducting risk assessments and designing, implementing or overseeing financial crime controls.

  • Hands-on design and implementation of FCC technology, including transaction monitoring rule development, tuning and CIP systems, and TM systems.

Skills and attributes

  • Analytical: understands complex product structures, workflows, transaction flows and data dependencies; analyzes issues independently and turns conclusions into actionable recommendations.

  • Regulatory interpretation: translates complex, evolving expectations into practical guidance, control requirements and executable plans.

  • Communication: excellent written, verbal and presentation skills; explains complex issues, risk decisions and metrics clearly to all levels, including senior management.

  • Collaboration and influence: works across functions and regions with positive intent, influences stakeholders and provides constructive, independent challenge.

  • Delivery: strong project, time and change management; prioritizes multiple initiatives under time constraints in a dynamic environment.

  • Mindset: strategic, inquisitive, proactive and solutions-oriented; anticipates emerging trends and favors sustainable control enhancement and appropriate automation.

  • Discretion: handles sensitive and confidential information and treats colleagues with compassion and respect.

How We Work

At Dakota, we value people who:

  • Strive for excellence

  • Practice extreme ownership.

  • Experiment fearlessly and learn quickly.

  • Stay close to customers.

  • Communicate clearly and directly.

What We Offer

  • Engaging problems that increase economic freedom globally

  • Competitive salary and equity

  • Remote work, no commuting to the office

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance

  • Regular team events and off-sites
descriptions.job-02j1zu7:
What is Kalshi?

Kalshi has defined a new category: prediction markets. Kalshi allows people to trade on the outcome of any events and turn any question about the future into a financial asset. Kalshi fought for years and legalized prediction markets in the US for the first time in history, is currently the fastest growing financial market in America, and has thousands of markets across politics, economics, financials, weather, tech, AI, culture and more.

We believe prediction markets have the potential to be the largest financial market because they turn anything into a financial position.

  • Our vision: well… build the largest financial market on the planet.

  • Our mission: bring more truth to the world through the power of markets.

Our culture is simple: we hire really talented people, work really hard, and enjoy the climb. We are looking for ambitious and exceptional people to join our (relatively small) team to help us build the next generation of financial markets.

Role Roadmap

As part of the Institutional Sales team at Kalshi, you'll identify, develop and onboard new institutional trading teams onto Kalshi. You'll guide them through integration and go-live, then own those relationships and provide the level of service sophisticated institutional customers expect. You'll be responsible for sourcing new trading firms, running institutional sales calls, managing a large pipeline, and working internally to solve onboarding and integration issues.

What You'll Do

  • Source and develop relationships with institutional trading firms that could trade on Kalshi

  • Own outbound prospecting across your existing network, LinkedIn and other traditional institutional sales channels

  • Run introductory and follow-up conversations with prospective trading teams

  • Build and manage a large pipeline of institutional relationships from initial outreach through activation

  • Guide customers through onboarding, integration and go-live, coordinating closely with Kalshi's Liquidity, Product and Operations teams

  • Develop deep relationships with the trading teams you bring onto the platform and provide exceptional ongoing service

  • Help troubleshoot integration questions, product updates, errors and other issues for institutional customers

  • Re-engage firms that have stalled during onboarding and help move them toward activation

  • Monitor customer activity and hold regular check-ins to understand needs, identify issues and drive deeper engagement

What You Bring

  • 2+ years of experience in institutional sales, financial services, brokerage, trading or another B2B financial-markets environment

  • Demonstrated ability to originate and develop new commercial relationships

  • Extremely strong professionalism and communication skills; you can credibly represent Kalshi with sophisticated institutional counterparties

  • High EQ and an ability to build trust quickly with a wide range of customers

  • Strong organizational skills and comfort managing a high-volume CRM and sales pipeline

  • Familiarity with financial markets and an ability to quickly learn derivatives and market structure

  • An existing network across proprietary trading firms, hedge funds, market makers, brokers or other institutional trading organizations

  • Experience helping institutional customers through technical integrations or onboarding

  • Familiarity with futures, derivatives, margin or clearing

  • Willingness to work in person from our New York office

Pay Transparency Disclosure

Salary Range: $130,000 - $200,000. This range reflects current market data for this role. Kalshi has minimal hierarchy and broad variance in experience levels within each title; if your compensation expectations exceed this range, we encourage you to reach out - we're always happy to discuss.

Our Culture

Meritocracy is at our core, and we value people who take ownership and figure (usually hard) things out. We dream big. We love our craft deeply and are proud of what we put out in the world. We are committed to our vision of building something big… but also useful: a product that brings more truth through the power of markets.

Kalshians are Kalshi’s most important asset: we pick Kalshians carefully, so we trust them fully on day 1.

Commitment to Equal Opportunity

Kalshi is committed to creating a culture of inclusion and belonging, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe it is our collective responsibility to uphold these values and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to join us in our mission. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law. If you are passionate about what you do and want to use your talents to support our mission and values, we’d love to hear from you.

We are looking for a talented Researcher who is excited by new and emerging technologies and can help move the organization forward by developing new capabilities, from design and proof of concept through production.

The position is office-based in Tel Aviv.


In this job, you'll:

AI at Chainalysis

You belong here.

descriptions.job-01y4wfj:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

We’re looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager to own the Public Sector market for Ardence, TRM’s AI-native investigation platform. Product marketing at TRM is organized as product PMM and market PMM. Product PMM owns platform positioning, differentiation, and launches across markets. Market PMM turns that foundation into growth within one market: understanding the buyers, running the sales and customer programs, and driving adoption and expansion. This is a market PMM role. You work closely with a Product Manager, Sales, and Customer Success. The PM builds, Sales opens doors, and you make sure buyers and existing customers know what Ardence can do for their missions and use it. AI handles the execution. You handle the judgment.

This role supports Defense and National Security customers as well as the rest of Public Sector. It requires U.S. citizenship and residence in the United States.

What you’ll own

You’ll own the Public Sector market position and growth programs for Ardence. Your buyers and users are investigators and analysts running complex, high-stakes cases for government agencies. Most Public Sector growth comes from existing customers, so a large part of the job is helping them use more of Ardence and expand into additional teams, workflows, and missions.

  • Public Sector positioning, messaging, demos, and sales materials built on the shared Ardence story

  • Defense and National Security positioning and programs, built with the teams that serve those agencies

  • Adoption and expansion programs for existing customers: which teams and missions could use more of TRM, what they would need to buy, and the stories, demos, and customer proof Sales and CS need to have that conversation

  • Customer marketing for Public Sector: finding customers who have capabilities they aren’t using, reaching the right users, and measuring whether usage changes

  • Mission-specific research and campaign content that supports both existing customer growth and new business

  • Follow-through on every launch in your market: did it reach the intended buyers, start qualified conversations, and get existing customers using what shipped

How you’ll work

Deep diving: You know the product at the level where you can demo it as well as anyone in the company. You know where the real value sits and where it breaks down. You’re in deal reviews and customer conversations often enough to know what lands, and you can hold a real conversation with both engineering and buyers.

Positioning: You take the shared Ardence story and make it specific to how government investigations run. You find the framing where a Public Sector buyer sees why TRM fits their mission, and you get claims agreed with Product at the start of a launch, not the night before.

Incepting: The story only works if the company carries it. You get Sales and CS telling it without you in the room, and you feed what you hear from agencies back to the product PMM and Product so the story and the roadmap improve.

Owning the moment: A launch, an enablement session, the materials a seller brings to an agency meeting. These are the moments where TRM either makes an impression or misses one. You own the narrative, the timing, and the outcome.

What we’re looking for

Storytelling. You think in narrative, not slides. You can make something technical matter to an agency buyer in two sentences, and your stories rest on customer signals, usage data, and win/loss patterns. You carry the same story across a one-pager, a demo, and an enablement session.

Commercial instincts. You understand what moves a deal and what moves an expansion, not just what sounds good in a deck. You’ve been in enough sales cycles to know the difference, and you’ve changed your positioning because of it.

AI builder. You build systems for the team, not just yourself. You’ve already offloaded repeatable work to automation, such as competitive monitoring, content generation, and usage reporting. Walk us through something you built that made the whole team faster.

Judgment. You know what good looks like and say so when it isn’t: a deck sellers aren’t using, a claim Product hasn’t confirmed, a launch that shipped without follow-through. You give feedback that moves things forward.

Customer-led measurement. You decide how to measure adoption and expansion, and you change the program when the numbers say it isn’t working.

Hard requirements

  • U.S.-only citizenship and residence in the United States

  • 5+ years in product marketing at a B2B SaaS company

  • You’ve owned at least two tier-one launches end to end: strategy, narrative, execution, and post-launch measurement

  • You’ve owned a website or major digital channel and made content decisions that moved pipeline, not just pageviews

  • You already use AI to build workflows and systems and can walk through a real example of something you built for your team, not just yourself

Deal breakers

  • Marketers who measure output in assets shipped

  • Anyone who treats AI as something to explore rather than something already running in their workflow

  • Candidates whose best examples inherited existing infrastructure. We need builders, not operators of programs someone else built.

About the team

TRM’s product team doesn’t coordinate work. It owns outcomes. Product marketers are embedded in the sales motion, in customer conversations, and in launch decisions. The team is small, the scope is real, and what you ship shows up directly in how deals close and how customers use TRM. PMMs here don’t wait to be asked. If the standard is slipping somewhere, you say so and help. AI is how we work, not just what we build.

If you do this well, existing Public Sector customers use more of Ardence, expansion conversations start from a story Sales and CS already carry, and TRM’s Public Sector market grows through the customers we already have.

What TRM speed looks like in this role

  • Sales asks for enablement on a new Public Sector program. You write the qualifying criteria and talk track, build a one-pager and slides, and run the enablement session that week.

  • A new capability ships. Within days you turn it into Public Sector messaging, a short demo, and a one-pager that Sales and CS can use with existing customers.

  • Usage data shows a customer is underusing Ardence. You turn it into an expansion story with the right demo and proof, and get it to the account team before their next conversation with the economic buyer.

The following represents the expected range of compensation for this role:

  • Individual pay is determined by skills, qualifications, experience, and location. The compensation details listed in this posting reflect the US base salary only.

  • The estimated base salary range for this role is $175,000 - $195,000.

  • Additionally, this role may be eligible to participate in TRM’s equity plan.

  • Please note – we factor in the different costs for geographies outside the United States.

Our R&D team is distributed not distant and will participate in work weeks, typically 1–2 times per quarter, at a TRM hub or other designated location. Work weeks may be scheduled with as little as 14 days’ notice, and some roles may require additional travel based on team and cross-functional needs. TRM coordinates and covers approved travel, lodging, and workspace.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Hut 8 is hiring a Finance partner to own the accounting for our data center development projects, from commitment and budget through cost capture, capitalization, and close. You will be the single point of accountability for what each project costs and how it is recorded: costs coded to the right budget line, capitalized correctly, and reconciled from the project ledger to the general ledger.

Project payables sit inside the role, so the person who accounts for the cost also controls how invoices are matched, approved, and paid. You will lead a team of project accountants, one per site, and work daily with Construction, Supply Chain, FP&A, Treasury, Legal, and Accounting.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Project Accounting

  • Own the WBS and cost-code structure for each project, and make sure every cost is coded to an approved budget line item.
  • Track committed, incurred, accrued, and paid cost against budget, contract value, and forecast for each project, and flag overruns early.
  • Incorporate change orders into commitments and budgets to ensure proper tracking.
  • Help prepare monthly project cost reports (budget vs. actual vs. forecast) and cost-to-complete forecasts with FP&A and project leadership.
  • Determine capitalization treatment (capitalize vs. expense) for project costs, and maintain CIP roll-forwards by project, including capitalized interest where applicable.
  • Support transfers from CIP to fixed assets when projects are placed in service, in coordination with Accounting.
  • Prepare month-end accruals for work performed but not yet invoiced, using percent complete, site progress, and retainage from Construction and Supply Chain.
  • Reconcile project cost ledgers and CIP to the general ledger, and keep the support for capitalized costs (contracts, POs, invoices, approvals) ready for quarterly reviews and audits.
  • Ensure adherence to SOX controls for each project.

Project Payables

  • Run commitment-based AP: match invoices to POs, subcontracts, and change orders while monitoring committed balances.
  • Own invoice-to-pay across multiple sites and legal entities, including urgent and off-cycle payments, and track retainage and lien waivers for construction vendors.
  • Complete AP subledger-to-GL and vendor statement reconciliations and aging reviews.
  • Onboard vendors, open bank accounts, and set up new legal entities with Treasury, Accounting, and Legal.

Team and Controls

  • Lead, coach, and prioritize the project accountants (one per site) through month-end close and high-volume payment cycles.
  • Design scalable processes and controls over project cost and payables (budget approval before commitment, PO matching, segregation of duties) in NetSuite and Ramp.
  • Report on project spend, accruals, and AP aging to leadership.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
  • 8+ years of progressive experience in project accounting, construction accounting, or accounting operations, including 5+ years leading a team.
  • Deep project cost accounting experience: WBS and cost coding, budget vs. actual reporting, cost-to-complete forecasting, and change orders.
  • Hands-on experience with capitalized costs and CIP, including capitalization policy and roll-forwards.
  • Experience with PO-driven, commitment-based AP (POs, subcontracts, change orders, retainage) across multiple legal entities and bank accounts.
  • Working knowledge of internal controls over procure-to-pay and capitalization.
  • Fluency in NetSuite and Ramp, and advanced Excel skills.
  • Clear communicator who can explain accounting requirements to non-finance teams such as Construction and Supply Chain.

Preferred Qualifications

  • CPA license.
  • Data center, energy, or infrastructure industry background.
  • Public company or SOX experience.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

To avoid the worst effects of climate change, most climate models agree the world will need to dramatically reduce emissions and remove 5-10 billion tons of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere per year by 2050. The Climate team’s goal is to accelerate Stripe’s path to net zero in parallel with the world’s. We do this by reducing Stripe’s emissions and leading initiatives to increase the likelihood we build sufficient carbon removal capacity to reach global climate goals.

In 2019, we developed the first measurement of Stripe’s emissions. In 2021 we launched Stripe Climate, enabling merchants to direct a fraction of their revenue to help scale emerging carbon removal technologies. In 2022 we launched Frontier, an advance market commitment to buy $1.8B+ of permanent carbon removal by 2040. In 2024, we entered our first multi-year offtake for clean energy.

Today, Stripe’s corporate net zero program is entering a new phase. We are looking to streamline our emissions measurement, create a template for catalytic emission reductions, and champion buying removals on the path to net zero, all while meeting our expanding global ESG disclosure requirements.

What you’ll do

As Stripe’s Climate Program Manager, you will set the strategy and lead the execution and reporting for Stripe’s corporate net zero program. You’ll partner with a wide range of stakeholders within and outside of Stripe – Accounting, Finance, Legal, Procurement, Facilities, Sales, and carbon accounting and assurance providers – to refine our greenhouse gas inventory, deliver a reduction and removal roadmap that meets our climate targets, and provide inputs to global ESG disclosures.

This role requires someone with expertise in carbon accounting and reductions strategy, sharp program and process management, a track record of getting big things done fast, and excellent judgement to make the ‘right’ recommendations for Stripe’s program.

Responsibilities

  • Net Zero strategy (~15%): Own and evolve Stripe’s corporate net zero strategy, including Stripe’s transition plan, priorities, budget, annual goals, emissions forecasts, removal retirements, and progress tracking. Stay current on evolving disclosure requirements, net zero guidance, and industry best practices to ensure Stripe’s program is high impact and best in class 
  • Emissions measurement (~30%): Build Stripe’s annual greenhouse gas inventory. Collect data inputs, evolve methodology, manage Stripe’s footprint vendors, run a rigorous and auditable process with cross-functional stakeholders, and identify opportunities to use AI to improve the process
  • Emissions reporting (~30%): Serve as Stripe’s subject-matter expert to deliver inputs to ESG controllership for regulatory disclosures and to customers for RFPs
  • Reduction program (~25%): Develop and manage emissions reduction initiatives across Stripe. This will include efforts like securing renewable electricity for Stripe’s scope 2 emissions, as well as supporting the creative and high-impact interventions like carbon removal or lower-emission data centers that we need to reach global net zero

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • BA or BS degree
  • 5-7+ years of experience in corporate sustainability, climate strategy, carbon accounting, environmental consulting, or a related field
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills – especially adept at translating complexity into clear recommendations 
  • A track record of generating and implementing ambitious emissions reduction initiatives
  • Strong quantitative skills and expertise in emissions accounting and Greenhouse Gas Protocol

Preferred qualifications

  • Has led a corporate climate program in a sector with a significant Scope 3 footprint, ideally technology or financial services
  • Is a self-starter, and has a proven track record of producing measurable reductions through clean energy, cloud usage, and other supplier engagement initiatives 
  • Has a working knowledge of major emissions accounting and climate reporting standards and requirements (e.g., CSRD, California SB 253, GHG protocol), and experience with Watershed or similar enterprise carbon management  platforms
  • Has experience partnering with cross functional controllership partners to manage a greenhouse gas inventory process that meets requirements for limited or reasonable assurance 
  • Is an exceptionally fast learner. Enjoys (and has experience) quickly ramping on new reduction technologies and sustainability standards

About Flowdesk

At Flowdesk, we are building the infrastructure powering the next era of global finance. As a full-service digital asset trading and technology firm, we provide liquidity solutions, OTC trading, and market infrastructure that connect digital assets to global markets with institutional-grade precision, transparency, and scale. Flowdesk combines expertise from traditional finance, algorithmic trading, and blockchain technology to deliver always-on trading capabilities across the digital asset ecosystem.

Founded in 2020, we have grown into a global team supporting institutions, exchanges, and token issuers worldwide as the financial system evolves toward tokenized markets.

You’ll be joining a company operating at the intersection of finance, technology, and crypto - solving complex market problems, building critical infrastructure, and helping shape how digital assets move globally. We move fast, think long term, and work with a strong ownership mindset across engineering, trading, product, operations, and business teams.

Research infra is a new team inside Technology, turning quantitative research into production by owning the research platform: the market-data store, the simulation framework, and the compute that lets quant researchers test thousands of hypotheses a day. Tick-level order-book data and our own execution traces stream through Redpanda into Delta Lake and ClickHouse. Two Quantitative Developer tracks make that platform fast (Research systems) and usable (Research tooling); this role adds the analytics that keep running when nobody is at the keyboard.

Mission

You’ll design and lead the agentic analytics of the platform. The first goal is to automate post-trade analysis (PTA): agents analyse every live strategy continuously, compare it with simulation, triage anomalies and write up what they find, while researchers review the conclusions. Once that loop is trusted, the agents move upstream to hypotheses and experiments. You’ll set the architecture, ship the first production agents yourself, and define the guardrails that keep automated analysis honest. You’ll work closely with quant researchers, traders and the risk team, as well as the Research systems and Research tooling engineers whose platform your agents run on.

Tasks

Automate post-trade analysis

  • Build agents that produce PTA for every live strategy leg on a schedule: P&L attribution, markouts, adverse selection, fill rate, inventory and fees.
  • Replace the notebooks and dashboards researchers maintain by hand today.

Compare simulation with reality

  • Replay live periods through the simulator and compare simulated fills and P&L with what actually happened, per strategy leg.
  • Flag drift before it costs a week of P&L.

Build monitoring with agentic triage

  • Turn PTA deltas, sim-vs-live drift, P&L, inventory and exposure into alerts.
  • Have agents triage them first, and hand a summary and recommended actions to the trader on call.

Plug agents into live data

  • Consume market data and execution logs from Kafka / Redpanda and query them in ClickHouse, so monitoring and research agents read data that is seconds old, not T+1.
  • Expose the platform as typed tools - for example an MCP server over the metrics library, data access and the simulator - so agents call the same validated code paths researchers do.

Make it production-grade

  • Version, test and deploy reports, datasets, prompts and agents through CI/CD (GitHub Actions, GitOps with Flux / Argo CD).
  • Land every agent output with its config, data snapshot and code version, so nothing it produces is unreproducible.

Evaluate the agents themselves

  • Build eval suites with known-answer tasks (planted anomalies, look-ahead traps) and track how often agents find, miss or fake them.
  • A regression in the eval suite fails the PR.

Later: from findings to hypotheses

  • Extend the loop upstream: agents draft hypotheses and campaign specs, run them on the simulation cluster, and a critic agent tries to break the result before a human sees it.
  • Build in the defences: trial budgets, multiple-testing corrections, untouched holdouts agents cannot read, and independent re-execution of every claimed result.

Ways of working

  • Ship through code review and CI like the rest of engineering - no exceptions for agent-authored code or prompts.
  • Document architecture decisions and the guardrails that keep automated analysis honest, so another engineer can operate the loop without you.
  • Own your systems end to end, from design through production monitoring and incident response.

How we’ll measure your impact

  • Researcher hours per week spent on PTA (down), and the share of live strategy legs with PTA that refreshes on its own.
  • Time from a live anomaly to a triaged summary in front of a trader.
  • Share of agent-reported findings that reproduce on independent re-execution.

Requirements

Must Have

  • 10+ years building production software or ML systems, including several years as a technical lead who set architecture for other engineers.
  • AI agents in production, not demos: multi-agent orchestration, tool calling, evaluation and red-teaming, cost and model routing, staged rollouts with a human in the loop.
  • Hands-on quantitative experience: you have built backtests, factor or signal models, or risk models, and have a healthy distrust of results that look too good - look-ahead bias, data snooping and regime change are second nature.
  • MLOps and CI/CD at platform level: you have built (not just used) model registries, experiment tracking, automated validation and deployment pipelines, and treat reproducibility as a hard requirement.
  • Streaming and analytical data systems in production: Kafka (or Redpanda) and ClickHouse, including schema design, partitioning, consumer lag and query performance at high volume.
  • Strong Python and SQL.
  • At ease on Linux and Kubernetes, with infrastructure-as-code for deploying and operating workloads.
  • Judgement to know which parts of research to automate, and which must stay with a human.

Nice to Have

  • Production experience in a systems language - Rust, C++ or Go - with Rust especially valuable, since the trading engine and simulator are written in it.
  • Experience in a trading environment, ideally market making, HFT or crypto.
  • Market microstructure knowledge: order books, queue position, markouts, adverse selection.
  • Open-weight model serving (vLLM, SGLang or similar) on your own GPUs.

Benefits

  • International environment (English is the main language)
  • Team events and offsites
  • Learning and Development budget
  • Health insurance for employee and legal dependents

Recruitment Process

Our process is consistent across all roles and is designed to assess genuine technical depth. Candidates should expect the following stages:

  • Stage 1 - Initial screening with TA (30 mins)
  • Stage 2 - Technical Screen - Meet the Data Director (45 mins)
  • Stage 3 - Quant Interview - Meet the Quant Developers and Quant Researchers teams (60 mins)
  • Stage 4 - Roundup Interviews - Meet the Infrastructure Director, the Data team, and the Chief Technology Officer (90 mins)

On the agenda, discussions rather than trick questions! These moments of exchange will allow you to understand how Flowdesk works and its values. But they are also (and above all) an opportunity for you to present your career path and your expectations for your next job!

We are committed to an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. If you require any reasonable adjustments or have specific needs to enable you to participate fully in the interview or assessment process (e.g., a sign language interpreter, extra time for a test, or an accessible location), please contact us to discuss how we can support you.
